private.text:
Bram plants himself just short of the top step, tests the first stone with his boot, and sets his shield toward the dark. He looks up at the worn carving, then back to you and Pell. "I'll go first. Watch the arch and the steps behind us. If that warm air turns sour, sing out."

Pell glances at the steps. "Warm air, clean steps. Someone's a better housekeeper than the entrance suggests." He crouches beside the threshold without crossing it, keeping clear of the middle of the entrance. "Give me a moment before we put weight on anything."

Bram puts his boot on the first step and leans his weight onto it slowly, shield angled toward the dark. The stone takes it. No grind, no shift. Warm air keeps rising past his shins, slow and even, the way heat comes off a banked forge.

Above you the lintel is hard to read. Rain and frost have worn the carving down to grooves no deeper than a fingernail. You stand at the edge of the moss with your head tipped back, and Bram runs his thumb along the stone beside you, slow, as if feeling for edges his eyes can't find.

At the threshold Pell squats on his heels, keeping out of the middle of the doorway, and starts on the stone.

Pell says, "Nothing I can find. Doesn't mean it's safe." He points out the arcs of dust on the steps. "Something sweeps its way along here. Might have just heard us."

He unhooks his hooded lantern. "Bram, I'll follow just behind you with the light. Slow going until we see the foot of these stairs."

Pell has the lantern open on his knee before you finish speaking. He pours the oil in a thin careful stream, strikes his flint, and gets the wick burning on the second try, then drops the hood. A thin blade of yellow light leaks out under the shutter and lies across the top step. Bram stays where he stood, one boot on the first stone, shield toward the dark.

You go down on your heels in the grass at the foot of the arch and part the moss and the long stems with the flat of your dagger. You work along the base of the stones, looking for a loaf of broken rock with letters on it.

Bram lets a long breath out through his nose, then turns his head just enough to speak to you and Pell without taking his eyes off the kobold.

"We'll go down, but we go slow, in our own order. Pell, you keep the lantern low and hooded and stay behind my shield arm. If I stop, you stop. Sefa, watch the walls and the turn of the stair behind us. No one opens anything until we've seen the Warm One face to face."

He shifts his shield forward and moves toward the first step, into plain view of the kobold but not into the light's full reach.

"Ixx. We'll come with you. You walk ahead of us, no more than ten feet, and you keep that broom down and your hands where we can see them. If the Warm One wants a door opened, then he'll tell us what's on the other side before we put a hand to it. And he'll tell us what became of the last ones who opened it." His voice carries down the stair, calm as a man negotiating a toll. "We're not thieves and we're not sacrifices. Three armed freehands, ready to deal. That's what you can tell him."

Pell lowers the lantern's shutter until its light falls at Ixx's feet rather than in his eyes, and sheathes his shortsword.

"No one's eating anyone, Ixx. I'm Pell. Doors are my trade, but I like to know what they're keeping apart before I open them."

He glances at you and the broken stone, then back to the kobold.

"The stone's face-up, yes. Does that cause trouble? And this door—is the Warm One behind it, or does he want something on the other side?"

Bram steps down onto the first stone. The sun is still warm on his back and on the iron rim of his shield, but his boots are already in the stair's shadow. Ixx's eyes follow the shield, then the half-drawn blade, and settle on Bram's face while the terms come down to him.

At "ten feet" the kobold looks at the steps between them as if he's counting them. At "keep that broom down" he looks at the broom. Then he lowers it until the twigs rest on the stone. "Broom is down when Ixx sweeps," he says, and he doesn't seem to mean it as a joke.

At "the last ones" his tail pulls tight round his ankle.

"Last ones did not open." It comes out fast and flat. Then slower: "Last ones are burned. Proper. Ixx's clan did it proper." His jaw shuts with a click, as if he'd like the words back. "Ixx tells the Warm One. Three… freehands. Ready to deal."

You lower your hand and sink onto your heels on the moss, until your eyes are nearer his. When you tell him you turned the stone and will put it back face-down, his whole body changes. His shoulders come down and his tail loosens a turn.

"Down," he says. "Before you go. Good." He looks at you for a long moment, the way you'd look at a lamp you weren't sure would hold.

Then you ask your questions, one after another, softly. While you ask, you watch the claws on the broom handle, the tail, and where his eyes go between the words.

Bram keeps his back to the cold room and his face to the heat. His voice comes down the aisle low and even, and it reaches the far end because nothing else in the room makes a sound: "If that white-gold is the lamp's kin, then Arren's warning stands: nothing of the fire goes up. We look, we learn, we don't carry it." He shifts his grip on the shield. "Keep clear of the chisel and the body until you've looked at both with the light low. If he's been dead since before the Warm One came, his boots may be the only honest thing in here." He pauses, then adds: "Call if that light brightens, or if the boots aren't empty. And Sefa, if your book goes warm again, you tell me, not after." After that he says nothing more. Out on the slope the orange stays where it is on the walls.

Pell crouches beside you, careful not to disturb the dead man's fist. "'Delivery.' Someone hired them to take something away. Dellmere, does that name mean anything to you?" He angles the lantern toward the paper in the dead man's coat. "I'll try the note. Leave his hand as it is for now." With fleece-wrapped fingers he gently tests the exposed edge of the paper. He keeps his voice low. "That last line could mean out of the room, out of the cellar, or out of his hand. Best not guess."

You hold your wrapped right fist a hand's width above his fist and watch.

The two lights don't mix the way two lamps would. Your Light is white and plain, a candle behind horn. The light between his fingers is warmer, white-gold, and it doesn't lean toward yours or shrink away. It goes on as if yours weren't there. The Book against your hip is warmer than it was at the door. It's the warmth of a cup held through cloth now, and it stays at that.

You look at it the way you were taught to look at a wound before you dress it, and work through what you know of wards and of the Faith.

Pell keeps the lantern held out and away from the smoking wool and says, "Bram—forward, slowly. Don't strike it." Pell reaches a wrapped hand toward the fleece at Bram's back, without tugging at his mail or stepping toward the vent. "Ixx, show us the safe way clear."

Bram doesn't flinch. The blunt stub comes on until it hangs a hand's width from his sleeve, and then he moves all at once. He gets his shield hand down to his hip, closes it on the smouldering fleece and pulls. The heat has already cooked the gut ties. The knot Pell tied at his back gives with a dry snap, and the wool comes away in his fist, greasy, hot and stinking. He drops it over the reaching arm.

Then, in the same breath, he has to get his sword arm behind his back, and that arm is the bare iron.

screens.text:
The session begins.

The afternoon sun lies flat and gold across the hillside, and the arch stands out of the grass like an old jaw. Past it, the steps fall away into the dark: the first dozen clear enough to count, then lost. Air comes up from below in a slow, even breath, warmer than it has any right to be, and carries a faint dry smell of stone and dust. The moss stops at the threshold. The top steps are worn smooth and almost bare, as though something has kept them clear. Above the arch, the carving on the lintel has weathered into shallow grooves; a patient eye might still make out a shape or two. Behind you, the land rolls back toward Beregost, a day's ride away. In front of you, the ruin waits, and whatever is at the bottom of it is waiting too. The light will hold for a few hours yet.

Your records:
Pell Dunmore — Human, rogue 5 (Thief), Lower City roof-runner turned hireling, level 5
HP 33/33 · AC 15 · Speed 30 feet
STR 10 · DEX 17 · CON 13 · INT 13 · WIS 12 · CHA 12
Skills: Stealth +9 (expertise); Sleight of Hand +6; Acrobatics +6; Perception +4; Investigation +4; Insight +4; Tools: thieves' tools +9 (expertise)
Saves: Dexterity saving throw +6 (proficient); Intelligence saving throw +4 (proficient); Strength saving throw +0; Constitution saving throw +1; Wisdom saving throw +1; Charisma saving throw +1
Attacks: Shortsword +6 to hit, 1d6+3 piercing; Dagger +6 to hit, 1d4+3 piercing, thrown 20/60; Shortbow +6 to hit, 1d6+3 piercing, range 80/320; Sneak Attack: +3d6 once a turn with advantage or an ally beside the target
Abilities: Proficiency bonus +3; Sneak Attack 3d6; Cunning Action: Dash, Disengage or Hide as a bonus action; Uncanny Dodge: a reaction halves the damage of an attack he can see; Fast Hands (Thief): a bonus action to use an object — a potion on another, a lock, a lamp; Second-Story Work: climbs at full speed; Thieves' Cant
Limits: Light armour; 33 hit points — he cannot stand at the front for long; Sneak Attack needs advantage or an ally beside the target
Counters: Hit dice 5/5
Money: 31 gp; 2 ep; 6 sp; 55 cp
Worn: Armor / clothing: Studded Leather Armour; Belt: Thieves' Tools; Main hand: Shortsword
Pack: Arrow ×20; Bedroll and Rations; Dagger ×2; Flask of Oil ×2; Hooded Lantern; Potion of Healing ×3; Shortbow; Silk Rope (50 feet)

Where you are: before the ruined arch on the hillside · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram plants himself just short of the top step and sets his shield toward the dark. He looks up at the worn carving, then back to Sefa and you. "I'll go first. Watch the arch and the steps behind us. If that warm air turns sour, sing out."

Sefa steps up to the arch but stops short of the threshold, where the moss ends. She tilts her head back to the lintel and runs her eyes slowly along the weathered grooves, one hand resting on the book at her belt. Without looking away from the carving, she speaks quietly: "Don't step past the moss yet. Something's kept those stairs clean, and it wasn't the wind." She breathes in the warm air rising from below and frowns. "That's not cave air. Too warm, too steady. Like a room someone's keeping heated."

After a moment she glances at Bram and you. "Give me a minute with this. If whoever built this left a warning or a name, I'd rather know before we go knocking. Pell, if you want to look over those top steps for anything nasty, I'll watch the dark." Her free hand stays loose at her side.

Bram puts his boot on the first step and leans his weight onto it slowly, shield angled toward the dark. The stone takes it. There is no grind and no shift. Warm air keeps rising past his shins, slow and even, the way heat comes off a banked forge.

Above him the lintel is hard to read. Rain and frost have worn the carving down to grooves no deeper than a fingernail. Sefa stands at the edge of the moss with her head tipped back, and Bram runs his thumb along the stone beside her.

At the threshold you squat on your heels, keeping out of the middle of the doorway, and start on the stone.

(A roll card for Pell Dunmore, your character. Only you press it.)

[Roll card] Pell Dunmore · Skill check — Investigation: reading the traces on the swept threshold and top steps
What adds to the die: +4 Investigation
DC 10
Rerolls left: 2
The die is cast on the server; tap it to see how it fell.

[Roll the die]

(A roll card for Pell Dunmore, your character. Only you press it.)

[Roll card] Pell Dunmore · Skill check — Investigation: reading the traces on the swept threshold and top steps
What adds to the die: +4 Investigation
DC 10
Rerolls left: 2
Die: 2
2 + 4 = 6
Failure — 6

[Onward] [Request an allowed reroll — Investigation: reading the traces on the swept threshold and top steps]

Your search turns up little. The stone is clean, too clean. The dust lies only along the edges and in the joints, brushed into long shallow arcs that overlap each other step after step down into the dark. Whatever made the tracks swept them away behind it. There are no wires and no hollow joints, and no stone sits higher or lower than its neighbours. Whatever kept these stairs clean left nothing you can read, except that it was thorough.

The warm breath keeps rising past you, and from somewhere far down in it comes a small dry sound. *Shhk. Shhk. Shhk.* It is slow and steady, like a broom on stone, and very far below. Then it stops.

Sefa keeps her free hand open and low at her side, eyes on the dark where the steps vanish. When the sweeping stops, nothing comes up into the light, and the stairwell stays empty and still.

Where you are: crouched at the side of the threshold · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Sefa doesn't move for a long moment. Her hand on the Book of Shadows tightens, and when she speaks her voice is a little too even.

"There's a lantern carved under the tower. Ring handle, one drop of flame." She swallows. "And a line cut later, in a hurry: *The light is lent, not given. What burns below...* and then the stone's broken off."

She looks down from the lintel to you and Bram. "Lent, not given. That's... close to home. Closer than I like." She doesn't explain, but she touches the prayer beads at her throat. "If whoever's down there knows that sign, they may know what I carry. That could open a door, or it could be the reason someone's waiting."

She glances at the stairwell and lowers her voice further. "And you heard that. Someone's tending the place. A broom doesn't stop on its own. It stopped because it heard us."

She crouches at the foot of the arch, still on the moss side. "Pell, anything on the steps? Bram, keep your eyes on the dark while I look. If that sweeping starts up again, or comes closer, tell me."

You have the lantern open on your knee before Sefa finishes speaking. You pour the oil in a thin careful stream, strike your flint, and get the wick burning on the second try, then drop the hood. A thin blade of yellow light leaks out under the shutter and lies across the top step. Bram stays where he stood, one boot on the first stone, shield toward the dark. He hasn't gone down, so you wait at the top with the lantern lit and hooded, ready to follow.

Sefa goes down on her heels in the grass at the foot of the arch and parts the moss and the long stems with the flat of her dagger. She works along the base of the stones.

On her third pass she stops two paces out from the left pillar, works the dagger point under something half sunk in the turf, and levers. A loaf-sized piece of broken stone comes up with a wet tearing of roots and rolls over into the light. Its face is cut with letters.

The hole where it lay is soft at the rim and pocked with small prints, no longer than a thumb, with three pointed toes and a fourth set back. They make a ring around where the stone lay. A tuft of coarse grey-white hair is caught on a burr of the left pillar at about knee height, and there is a smell of goat. Your lantern-light lies across all of it.

Then, from below, the broom starts again. *Shhk. Shhk. Shhk.* It keeps the same slow, patient rhythm, but it is much closer now. It isn't at the bottom of the stair any more. It is somewhere in the dark just past where the steps run out of light, and it is coming up.

Your records, changed:
Carried: + Flask of Oil; − Flask of Oil ×2

Where you are: top of the stair under the arch, lantern lit · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram backs off the first step and moves to the side of the arch, out of the lantern's line, so his shadow won't fall down the stair. His shield comes up and his sword is half out of the scabbard in an instant. "That's no wind and no rat," he says, low, pitched to carry only a few feet. "Pell, light the way, but stay behind me. Sefa, the stone—" he glances at the writing. "Read it if you can. But be ready to move."

Sefa rises from the grass with the stone wedge still in her hands. Her lips move once over the words, then she reads them aloud, low and quick: "*The light is lent, not given. What burns below is kept, not killed. Let nothing of the fire go up.* Signed Arren." She sets the wedge gently against the left pillar, writing face-up. "It's not a curse. It's a keeper's warning. Someone's guarding a fire down there, and they don't want it brought out."

She nods at the ring of small clawed prints round the hollow and at the tuft of goat hair caught on the pillar, and you see them both. "Little things with claws came to look at this and didn't dare touch it. And a goat, or something that smells like one." She lets out a breath. "Not much of a welcome party."

She steps onto the moss at Bram's shoulder, not past him, and raises her empty left hand palm-out toward the dark. Her right hand stays low and open. "Nobody loose anything unless it comes at us," she murmurs. "It's sweeping, not charging. Pell, don't throw light down there yet. Keep it hooded."

The light falls down the stair in a long yellow wedge, past twenty steps and then thirty, and lands on something small.

The three of you call down one after another. Bram goes first, flat and unshaken: "We mean no harm to whoever keeps this place. We're armed, and there are three of us. If you're a spirit, say so. If you're flesh, speak. If you're neither, you'd best slow your broom." Then Sefa, in a clear, calm voice: "Hello below. We've read Arren's words on the stone. We've come to talk, not to carry anything off. Will you come up to the light and speak with us, or shall we wait here?" Then you. The sweeping stops before you finish.

About forty feet down, where the lantern light fades, a kobold stands on the stair with a broom in both claws. He's no taller than Bram's belt. His scales are the dull red of old brick, flaking grey at the snout. He wears a sack-cloth apron, and his broom is a bundle of twigs bound with coarse grey-white hair, the same hair that's caught on the pillar. He has one foot on the step above, about to climb, and he holds there with his head ducked and his eyes screwed half shut against the lantern.

He doesn't come any closer. The afternoon sun lies across the top of the stair and the threshold, and he looks at that gold band of light the way a man looks at a fire he has to walk through.

"Flesh," he says at last. His Common is thin and careful, every word pressed out on its own. "Ixx is flesh. Small flesh. Not much eating on Ixx."

He holds the broom crosswise in front of him like a bar across a door. His tail has wrapped itself round his ankle.

"You read the stone." It isn't a question. His slit eyes go to Sefa and stay on her. "Ixx heard. Arren's words." He hisses through his teeth, a short wet sound. "The stone lay with its face in the ground. Good. Asleep. Now its face is up?"

He waits for an answer to that. When none comes fast enough he shakes himself, like a dog shedding water, and starts again in a voice that sounds recited.

"Ixx is sent. The Warm One hears feet at the door. He says: tall ones with hands, come down. There is a door the Warm One wants open. Hands that open it, he pays well. Gold. Old gold, from before." His claws tighten on the broom handle. "He says it nicely. Ixx says it nicely too."

He glances back over his shoulder, down into the dark he came from. You've watched a lot of runners give messages they didn't write, and this is what it looks like. The kobold said *open* with his eyes somewhere else.

"Come down, Ixx shows the way. Ixx sweeps in front, you walk on clean stone." His snout turns from Bram's shield to Sefa's raised hand and on to your lowered blade. "Or you go away, and Ixx sweeps the steps where you stood. Both is all right. Only..." he stops himself, then says it anyway, quickly: "only put the stone's face back down, if you go."

He stays on the step below the sunlight, broom held across his body, and waits for you to answer.

Your journal, new:
+ Goal: The Warm One's door
+ Quest: The Warm One's door

Where you are: just outside the stairway with the lantern · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram lets a long breath out through his nose, then turns his head just enough to speak to you and Sefa without taking his eyes off the kobold.

"We'll go down, but we go slow, in our own order. Pell, you keep the lantern low and hooded and stay behind my shield arm. If I stop, you stop. Sefa, watch the walls and the turn of the stair behind us. No one opens anything until we've seen the Warm One face to face."

He shifts his shield forward and moves toward the first step, into plain view of the kobold but not into the light's full reach.

"Ixx. We'll come with you. You walk ahead of us, no more than ten feet, and you keep that broom down and your hands where we can see them. If the Warm One wants a door opened, then he'll tell us what's on the other side before we put a hand to it. And he'll tell us what became of the last ones who opened it." His voice carries down the stair, calm as a man negotiating a toll. "We're not thieves and we're not sacrifices. Three armed freehands, ready to deal. That's what you can tell him."

Sefa lowers her raised hand slowly, palm still open. She doesn't step forward into the band of sun; she crouches on the moss instead, bringing herself nearer the kobold's height, and keeps her voice gentle.

"Thank you, Ixx. You said it nicely." She nods toward the wedge propped against the pillar. "The stone's face is up because I turned it. I wanted to know what it said. I'll put it back down before we go, whichever way we go. You have my word on that."

She glances once at you and Bram, a small look, then back to the kobold.

"Before we come down, help me understand, so we don't open the wrong thing. Who is the Warm One? Is he the fire Arren wrote about, or is he the one keeping it?" A pause. "And this door he wants opened. Is it a door *in*, or a door *out*?"

She watches the kobold closely while she speaks.

"One more thing, Ixx. Who was Arren? Did you know him? Did the Warm One?" Softer still: "And you. Do *you* want that door open?"

Quietly, without turning her head, she adds for you and Bram: "The stone says keep the fire below. Something below wants a door opened and pays in old gold. I'd like to know which side of that door we'd be standing on."

Bram steps down onto the first stone. The sun is still warm on his back and on the iron rim of his shield, but his boots are already in the stair's shadow. Ixx's eyes follow the shield, then the half-drawn blade, and settle on Bram's face while the terms come down to him.

At "ten feet" the kobold looks at the steps between them as if he's counting them. At "keep that broom down" he looks at the broom. Then he lowers it until the twigs rest on the stone. "Broom is down when Ixx sweeps," he says, and he doesn't seem to mean it as a joke.

At "the last ones" his tail pulls tight round his ankle.

"Last ones did not open." It comes out fast and flat. Then slower: "Last ones are burned. Proper. Ixx's clan did it proper." His jaw shuts with a click, as if he'd like the words back. "Ixx tells the Warm One. Three… freehands. Ready to deal."

Sefa sinks onto her heels on the moss, until her eyes are nearer his. When she tells him she turned the stone and will put it back face-down, his whole body changes. His shoulders come down and his tail loosens a turn.

"Down," he says. "Before you go. Good." He looks at her for a long moment, the way you'd look at a lamp you weren't sure would hold.

Then she asks her questions, one after another, softly, watching the claws on the broom handle, the tail, and where his eyes go between the words.

"Who." He works his jaw. "The Warm One is big. Old gold. What he is, Ixx does not say. The Warm One likes to say it himself."

"Not the fire." That one comes easily. "Fire is under. Old. Before everything. The Warm One came down to it, when Ixx was small."

When she asks whether the door leads in or out, he doesn't answer at first. He looks back down the stair into the dark. Then he climbs, three steps, four, up to the last shadowed step below the band of sun, close enough that he doesn't have to raise his voice. He keeps it low anyway.

"Out."

To her question about Arren he gives a short wet hiss. "Arren is words. On the stone. Below, on the door, same words. The Warm One knows them. He says the name when he is angry. Knew Arren? No. Arren is before. Only words now."

Her last question gets nothing for a long while. When the answer comes it is very quiet, so quiet that even Bram, a few feet above him, barely catches it.

"The Warm One cannot go up. Ixx goes up for him. The Broom goes up. Goats, news, tall ones." His claws shift on the handle. "When the door opens, nobody sweeps for him anymore."

He says nothing after that.

You have already turned the shutter down until the light pools on the stone at the kobold's feet. For the first time Ixx opens his eyes all the way, and the first thing he looks at is your empty hand, the sword back in its sheath.

"Pell," he repeats, trying out the name. "Doors." To the question about the stone he answers: "Face-up, elders say it is awake. Awake stone, elders get loud. All night loud." His eyes flick to Sefa and back. "But it goes down. She says." To the other question: "Behind. The Warm One is behind the door. Other side is only up."

Then he takes the broom in both claws, turns, and goes back down until he is about ten feet below Bram's boot. He puts the twigs to the stone and sweeps the same step over and over, *shhk, shhk*, waiting for you to follow.

Arren's wedge still leans face-up against the left pillar in the sun.

Your journal, new:
+ Promise: Arren's stone face-down

Where you are: at the top of the stair with the hooded lantern · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram falls in behind Ixx without taking his eyes off the little figure, shield low across his body and sword still in hand, not sheathed. "Pell, light at his feet and the step ahead of me, nothing more," he says quietly. "Sefa, you're our eyes behind. If the air thickens or the walls stop being plain stone, say so." Then, aimed at the kobold's back: "Ixx. We're coming. You stop when I tell you, and we stop when the Warm One says stop. Ten feet, no more." He doesn't look back at the wedge of stone by the pillar, but his jaw is set. "And we'll leave that stone face-down before we leave here, no matter which way it goes." Ixx looks up at "ten feet, no more" and sets his broom to the next step down.

Sefa gets to the stone first. She kneels at the left pillar, rolls Arren's wedge onto its face and presses it back into its hollow, inside the ring of little prints, and smooths the turf round its edges with her palm. "There," she says down to Ixx. "Asleep again. Your elders can have a quiet night." Then, softer: "I've read it. I won't forget what it said." Below the sunlight, Ixx watches every bit of it with his head cocked. When she says *asleep again*, his tail lets go of his ankle all at once.

You said you'd see to the stone, but it's already down when you reach it. You crouch, tip it a finger's width to check the letters are against the earth, and let it settle. Then you stand up and take your place behind Bram's shield arm, with the lantern hood dropped so the light lies on the step and no farther.

Sefa dusts off her hands, comes back to the head of the stair and stops at Bram's shoulder. She speaks low, too low to carry ten feet down. "Here's what I read in him. The Warm One's sealed in behind that door, and the door leads *out*. Arren's words are on it too. Ixx isn't afraid of his master, he's proud of him. What scares him is the door opening. His clan lives by serving whatever's down there, and if it gets loose they're nothing to it. Or worse." She glances at the lintel. "*Old gold, from before.* Big, warm, and talks fancy. I'd bet my beads it's a dragon, or something that thinks like one." She meets Bram's eyes, then yours. "We go down and we listen. We don't open anything, not for any amount of gold, until we know what Arren shut in and why. The stone says *let nothing of the fire go up*. I'm inclined to take a dead man's word over a live dragon's."

She takes her place behind you both, watching the walls and the stair at your backs, one hand on the Book of Shadows. Before she steps down she calls gently to the kobold: "Ixx, sweep on. We're coming. And when we reach the bottom, tell me one more thing if you can: what does your clan do, if the Warm One gets angry with *us*?" As you descend you can hear her counting the steps under her breath.

When you thank him, Ixx stops sweeping. He stands with the twigs on the stone and looks up at you as if he'd been handed something and doesn't know which pocket it goes in. Then he bows too low and too fast, and starts sweeping again.

---

The stair goes down a long way.

For the first thirty steps it's cut straight into the hill. The walls are rough grey rock, and roots hang through the cracks overhead. Then the rock stops. The raw stone gives way to dressed blocks, squared and fitted without mortar. Every so often one carries a mason's mark the size of a thumbprint, a little tower like the one on the lintel. The steps get wider and more even here. This part was built, not dug.

There are niches set into the wall every dozen steps, at shoulder height. Each is black with old soot, and in a few of them sits a stub of greasy kobold-made candle, cold. Goat droppings have been swept into the corners of the landings in tidy little heaps. Somebody comes back for those, too.

It gets warmer the whole way. By the eightieth step the air is dry enough to catch in the throat, like the air in a bakehouse before dawn. It doesn't smell of smoke, only of hot stone and dust. Far below, under the sound of the broom, something too low to hear makes the stair hum very faintly underfoot, the way a floor does above a working mill.

Then the steps end.

The bottom is a landing of the same dressed stone, about twenty feet across, roofed with a low vault. Iron rings for lamps are set into the walls. They're rusted and empty. Two ways lead off it.

Straight ahead, a wide passage slopes on down. The warm breath comes up out of it, and so does the hum. Far down at its end, past where your light can reach, there's a dull orange smudge on the dark, like the glow of a forge seen through a shutter.

To the left, a hole has been knocked through the wall at about the height of Bram's chest. It's rough-edged and kobold-sized, and it opens on a tunnel with a dirt floor. It smells of goat, tallow and a lot of bodies living close together. As your boots touch the landing, a noise comes out of it: many thin voices, high and quick, all talking over one another. Then one of them barks a word, and they go dead quiet. In that quiet you can feel them listening.

Ixx leans his broom against the wall. He turns to Sefa and answers the question she gave him at the top, quietly, the way he said the true thing before.

"Warm One angry, clan does what he says. Slings. Teeth. Clan is many." He glances at the hole in the wall, and his tail creeps back round his ankle. "Ixx asks you. If he is angry, not in there. Little ones in there."

Then he straightens his apron and gives you the next part of the message as if it had been there all along.

"Here Ixx goes ahead. Tells the Warm One: three freehands, ready to deal. Tells him he says first what is behind the door, and what of the last ones." He looks at Bram for that. "The tall ones wait here, on the landing. Or in the warren, with the elders, by the fire. Elders want to see who turned the stone." His eyes go to Sefa and stay there. "Ixx comes back. Not long."

He waits with one claw on the broom handle, looking from Bram to the sloping passage and back. He's ready to go when you let him, and he won't go before.

Where you are: the landing at the foot of the stair · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram keeps his sword low but not sheathed. He shifts his weight, plants his feet where the vault covers him, and glances once at the dark mouth of the warren before he answers Ixx.

"We'll wait here on the landing. Not in the warren. Old road habit: you don't set your back to a wall you haven't walked around yet." He says it plainly, like a rule of weather, not a threat. "Go and tell the Warm One we came down because you asked us to. Three freehands, ready to deal. Tell him we won't put a hand to the door until he tells us, straight, what's behind it and what happened to the last. If the elders want to see us, they can come out here where I can see the stair."

He turns his head slightly toward you and Sefa without taking his eyes off the two ways ahead. "Pell, hood the lantern down, light on the floor. Let them see we're not prying into every corner. Sefa, watch the warren's mouth and our backs. I'll watch the passage."

Then, to Ixx, a little softer: "Take your broom. You can leave it here if they'll fret over it, but it's your tool and I won't keep a man from his work. Tell him I said we leave the door shut unless he gives us good reason." He pauses. "Good reason means the truth, not the gold first."

Sefa looks at the hole in the wall for a long moment, then nods to Ixx. "Go on, Ixx. Tell him just as you said. We'll be here when you come back." She adds, gently: "And if he's angry, we won't bring it in there. Not near the little ones. You have my word on that too."

Bram is set under the lip of the vault, where the roof covers him and the stair is at his back. The warren's hole is on his left and the sloping passage runs straight ahead. His sword stays low and bare. Ixx listens to all of it with his head cocked, the way he listened at the top.

When Bram tells him the broom is his tool and nobody will keep him from his work, the kobold looks at the broom leaning against the wall, then up at Bram, as if he's been told something about it he didn't know. He picks it up in both claws.

"Broom goes. Ixx sweeps in front of the Warm One. Always." Then he says the end of the message again under his breath, slowly, setting the words in order to carry. "Truth. Not gold first."

Sefa's promise about the little ones seems to hit him harder than Bram's terms. He looks at the hole in the wall, then at her, and gives two quick, low bobs of his head. When you say you want no fight among the little ones, Ixx bobs again, a little smaller.

"Ixx tells. Not long."

He goes down the sloping passage, and he sweeps even with nobody behind him. *Shhk, shhk*, one stride at a time, the sound getting thinner. The small shape goes down against the orange smudge until you can't tell it from the dark. Then the sweeping is lost under the hum.

You take the stair-side edge of the landing and turn the lantern's shutter so the light pools on the flagstones, away from the warren. From there you can see the hole, the passage and the stair, and Bram is a word away. You say your piece about keeping the stairs clear, low enough that it stays on the landing.

Sefa keeps her voice low to you and Bram. "The elders want to see who turned the stone. I think I should go. They've lived beside this fire and those words their whole lives. They'll know what Arren's door says, and what the Warm One says about it when he's angry. I'd rather hear that before we stand in front of him than after." She glances down the sloping passage at the orange smudge. "Bram, you hold the landing. It's the only way back up, and if Ixx comes back or anything else comes up that slope, you'll see it first. Pell, will you come with me as far as the hole? Stand where you can see me and still shout to Bram. I'll keep it short."

She draws nothing and unclips nothing. The Book stays on her belt and her hands are empty and in plain sight. At the hole she stops on the landing side, crouches so her head is lower than the opening, and speaks in through it, soft and clear:

The dagger goes back into its sheath, and when she tugs at it nothing knocks. She runs her palm down the front of her studded leather, feeling for studs that could click against each other or catch on a wall, and tucks a fold of the fleece under her belt over the worst of them.

The rest of the fleece doesn't want to tear. The hide is old and stiff with grease, and she has to set her teeth in it and pull with both hands before it gives along the edge with a dull rip. She spits twice. In the end she has two ragged strips, and she holds one out to you.

"For the paper room. Kesh says a little one went in and came out grey to the elbows, and stayed grey for a tenday. Wrap your hands before you touch anything in there, and don't breathe it in. You'll be touching more than I will."

She checks that the Book sits quiet at her belt and gives you the order of march in a low voice. Ixx sweeps in front, then Bram, then you with the light low, and she goes last. You step where the broom steps and nobody stops near a hole in the floor. At the black door on the left you go in, and Ixx can wait or come as he likes. "If he balks, we let him tell his master. I'd rather the Warm One knew we'd gone in than have Ixx lie for us and pay for it."

*(Out of game: Sefa came out of the warren at the end of last round, so she is already on the landing with you and Bram. There's nobody inside to wait on. Your "understood" is taken as your answer to her "Ready?", and Bram still has the moment before Ixx arrives to stop or change anything.)*

Sefa steps to the head of the slope with her hands empty and pitches her voice to carry on the stone and no further.

"Ixx. We've sat with the elders, and we're wrapped. Come up and sweep for us, please."

At the hole behind her, the candle at the edge of the dark draws back a hand's width and stays there.

The answer comes sooner than you expect. *Shhk, shhk.* The broom is already well up the passage, as if Ixx had been waiting partway down rather than at the bottom. It climbs fast, faster than he has swept so far.

He comes up into the pool of lantern light and stops ten feet below the landing. He holds the broom crosswise and stays there with his eyes on the fleeces. He takes in Bram's shoulders and hip, the wrapped javelins, your daggers and Sefa's knife, and his nostrils work. For a moment he looks very nearly proud of you all.

Then the recited voice comes, word laid on word.

"The Warm One counts. He says: *elders talk long.* He says: *the Warm One is patient.*" Ixx swallows. "He says *patient* two times."

His tail has wound itself round his ankle. He waits a breath, but there's no more message, and when he speaks again it's in his own voice.

"Ixx sweeps. Down now?"

Where you are: the landing at the head of the slope · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram takes up his shield and steps to the head of the slope, just behind the edge of Sefa's lantern-light. He rolls his shoulders once, and all that comes from under the fleece is the soft rub of wool on wool. He gives Ixx a single nod.

"Down now. Ixx, you sweep ahead of us—same as before, ten feet, no more. You stop where the broom stops. We don't pass you."

He glances back once at you and Sefa. "Order as she set it. I'm behind the broom. Pell, light low and on the floor, not on the walls. Sefa, last, and keep two steps between you and Pell. If I say *hold*, we all hold. If I say *back*, we turn on the spot we're standing and walk out at my pace. No one runs."

Then, quieter, to Ixx: "Tell him we're on our way. And Ixx—if the brood's watching, keep them off the foot of the stairs behind us. We don't want little feet near that long room." He sets his shield toward the dark. "Lead on."

Sefa takes a second strip of fleece from her belt and presses it into your free hand without a word. Then she crouches at the lip of the slope, low beside Ixx so she isn't standing over him.

"Down now, Ixx. Thank you for coming so quickly." Her eyes go to his tail, wound round his ankle, and her voice stays gentle. "Two times patient. We heard."

She lets out a breath before she goes on, and she says it plainly. "There's a black door on the left, before the long hot room. The wardens' room. We're going to stop there first and look inside. Only look, and we'll be careful with our hands." She holds his eyes. "You don't have to come in. You can wait at the door, or go on and tell the Warm One where we are. If he asks, tell him the truth: the stone-turner wanted to see the wardens' room before the wardens' door. That's mine to answer for, not yours."

She rises, takes her place at the back of the line behind you, and looks once over her shoulder at the hole in the wall. "Sweep on, Ixx. We'll step where you step."

---

Ixx takes Bram's order the way he takes a message, mouthing the words as he hears them. When Bram asks him to keep the brood off the foot of the stair, he answers without stopping to think.

"Little ones do not go down the slope. Never. Kesh keeps them." He looks at the hole in the wall. "Kesh hears you anyway."

At the edge of the hole the candle goes out of sight.

When Sefa tells him about the black door, Ixx goes completely still. His claws close on the broom handle, and air leaks out between his teeth in a short, wet hiss.

"Wardens' room." He says it under his breath, the way Kesh said *Arren*. "He cannot see in there. Cannot hear in there." His eyes go down the passage toward the orange smudge and back to her. "Ixx does not go in."

The next part takes him longer. "Ixx tells true. Stone-turner wants to see. Stone-turner answers." He tries the words over once more under his breath, and that seems to settle him. His tail stays wound round his ankle, but the rest of him no longer looks braced to run. "Ixx does not have to make words up. Good."

When you say the same thing in your own plain way, that you won't ask him to hide it, Ixx gives you a small bob of the head and turns to the slope.

*Shhk, shhk.* You go down.

The passage is ten feet wide and built like the lower stair: dressed blocks fitted without mortar, with the little tower cut low on a stone every so often. The slope is gentle, but it never levels off. A shallow groove runs down the middle of the floor, worn by a lot of feet over a lot of years, and that is where Ixx sweeps. Bram keeps ten feet behind him. You come next with the lantern shutter down, and the light makes a yellow pool round your boots that reaches no farther than the stone just ahead. Sefa walks two steps behind you, counting under her breath.

The heat climbs as you go. Before long the air is like a bakehouse with the oven doors open. The hum gets louder too. You don't hear it so much as feel it coming up through the soles of your boots. The walls have shoulder-height niches like the stair, but no kobold has left a candle in any of them here.

About a hundred and fifty feet down, the left-hand wall changes.

A door is set into it under a squared arch. It's broad and made of oak, and the oak is charred black all over, crazed into little squares like a log pulled out of a fire. It still stands, and it's shut. Its three hinges are dull green with age: bronze, not iron. Over the arch is a single carving, a lantern with a ring handle and one drop of flame, and no tower above it this time.

At hand height on the door's edge there's a smear. It's a palm-print, darker than the char around it, with four fingers dragged down from it, as if someone pushed the door shut behind him while he was going down. The door doesn't sit flush. There's a gap the width of a finger between its edge and the jamb.

Air comes out of that gap, and it's cool, the first air in the whole cellar that hasn't been warm. It brushes your knuckles round the lantern handle and smells of old paper and nothing else.

Beyond the door the passage keeps sloping down. At the far edge of the light, forty feet or so on, the orange starts to show on the walls.

Ixx stops ten feet short of the door, as he was told. He won't look at the lantern carved over the arch.

"Here. Black door." He shifts the broom from one claw to the other. "Ixx goes. Tells. Stone-turner looks at wardens' room." He hesitates. "When tall ones come out, call down. Ixx comes, sweeps the long room. Ixx knows where the holes sleep light."

He turns and goes down toward the orange, sweeping the whole way. The sound of the broom thins and blurs, and the hum swallows it.

The three of you stand at the black door, the lantern pool at your feet and cool air coming out of the gap. Nobody has touched the door.

Where you are: at the charred black door, sloping passage · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram stops at the edge of the cool air and lets it run over his face before he moves.

"Hold." He doesn't take his eyes off the door. "Pell, look at the edge and the hinges before we put hands on it. The print says someone shut it from the inside as he went down—or was dragged down and threw his hand back for purchase. I want to know if it's wedged, barred, or watched."

He angles his shield across his body and sets himself between the door and the slope. "Sefa, keep the light off the walls and watch the passage. If that orange flutters or Ixx stops sweeping, call it." He pauses. "And if this is the room Kesh won't walk into, we don't leave anyone alone inside it. Two in, one at the door always. The one at the door stands where I stand now, facing out."

Then he turns and plants himself facing out, toward the orange glow at the far edge of the light. He says it once and leaves it there.

Sefa winds a strip of fleece round her right hand, wool inward, and ties it off with her teeth. She looks at the dragged palm-print for a moment, then answers your question from the slope, low:

"What else Kesh told me: the paper in there falls to grey at a touch. It's old burning, from before the Warm One. The fourth man called out for two nights from inside, the same tall-folk words over and over, and then stopped." She nods at the print. "That's likely him, shutting the door behind himself. And she said one more thing: *back to the lamp, stone-turner, not past it.* If we find what he carried, it goes back where it came from. Nowhere else."

She glances down the slope, then up at the lantern carved over the arch, with no tower above it this time.

"Bronze hinges. No iron in this door at all. Whoever built this room didn't want it to ring." She breathes in the cool air from the gap. "And it's cold in there. The only cold place in the whole cellar."

She steps back half a pace to give you the door. "Pell, it's your trade. Look it over before anyone pushes, top to bottom. If it's clean, open it slowly, a hand's width at a time. Bram, watch the slope, not the room."

Behind you all the hum is going, like a mill heard through a thick wall.

Sefa bends to the finger-wide gap, keeping her face off the char, and listens. Then she speaks into it, the way you'd speak at the curtain round a sick bed: "We're coming in. We mean no harm to whoever's within, living or dead. We've come for what was taken from the door, and to put it back."

Nothing answers her.

---

You crouch with the lantern raised a little, your face turned away from the opening, and go over the door from the top down. This is your trade, and the door doesn't hide much from you.

There's no lock on it and never was. A bronze ring on the outside serves for a pull, green like the hinges. The jamb has no catch, no wire and no pin-hole, and none of the joints along the threshold are loose. Through the gap, by the lantern, you can make out a bronze bracket on the inside of the jamb, the kind a drop-bar sits in. Its twin will be on the far side. The bracket is empty. Either nobody barred this door from within, or nobody could.

Ash has drifted along the threshold, fine and pale grey, like hearth-sweepings. The draught out of the gap has blown it into a little ridge against the stone. It lies on your side of the sill as well, a hand's width out into the passage.

The door is clean as far as you can tell. You wind the fleece strip round your left hand, take the ring in your right, and lift as you push so the foot of the door won't drag. It swings inward, a hand's width and then another. The bronze turns stiffly, with one low dry note as the hinges give, and then it opens without a scrape.

Sefa raises her wrapped hand and touches two fingers to the fleece. Light wells up in the wool, steady and white like a candle behind horn, and spreads out from her fist into the doorway.

---

The room is longer than it is wide, perhaps forty feet deep and half that across. The shelves Kesh described run back in rows from the door, dark oak twice Bram's height, and every shelf is full. The books still stand in their places, spines out, packed shoulder to shoulder. They're all black. They look like logs pulled whole out of a fire: they've kept their shape, but every edge is crazed and soft-looking, and nobody would want to breathe near them.

Ash covers the floor an inch deep, grey and level as new snow, except where it has been walked through.

There's one line of tracks. Hobnailed boots go in from the threshold, wavering, and one foot drags in a long furrow, step after step, down the middle aisle between the shelves.

Something lies in the ash just inside the door, a pace to the left, where a man would drop whatever he held to free his hand for the door. It's a chisel as long as a forearm, of black iron gone dull, with a mushroomed striking head. Nothing has settled on it. Its own fall has thrown the ash back from it in a little ring.

The tracks go on past the reach of Sefa's light and your lantern, to the far end of the room.

Down there, between the last two shelves and low near the floor, there's another light. It's faint, no stronger than a coal seen through a cupped hand, and it isn't the colour of Sefa's or of the lantern. It's paler than either, a white-gold, like the top step at evening. At the very edge of where the light gives out, two boot soles are turned toward the door, their hobnails catching a gleam.

Nothing moves in there, and no ash stirs.

Out on the slope, in front of Bram's shield, the orange glow stays where it is, and nothing comes up the passage.

*(Out of game: no roll was needed. Checking a door is your own trade, and there was nothing hidden on it to find.)*

Where you are: at the threshold of the burnt library, holding the door · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Sefa keeps her glowing fist low, angled at the floor, and speaks over her shoulder in a breath.

"Chisel's just inside, on the left. Nobody touch it, nobody kick it. It's the one thing in here that could ring." A pause. "Tracks go all the way to the back. There's a light down there, white-gold, like the lamp Kesh drew. And boots. I think he's still here."

She lays her free hand flat on the Book at her hip for a moment. "And this went warm when the door opened. It hasn't done that before. I don't know yet if that's good."

She pulls the loose end of her fleece up over her nose and mouth and ties it behind her head.

"Bram, door, facing out, as you said. Pell, with me, two paces behind. Walk in his prints, in the furrow where the ash is already broken. Don't brush the shelves. If anything falls, let it fall."

Then she goes in. She steps wide of the chisel on her right and sets her boots down inside the dead man's prints. You come two paces behind her and put your feet where hers have been. Bram stays at the door with his shield across his body, facing down the slope.

The air in here is cold enough to raise the skin on your arms after the slope. It's still. Your steps make no echo, as if the shelves soak up the sound. The black books stand packed on both sides, as tall as two men, and in the light their spines look as soft as wet bread. Halfway down, a crumb of char drops from a high shelf without anyone touching it and lands in the ash with no sound at all. Neither of you stops for it.

There is one line of tracks in the ash and no second set. Every shelf-end you pass is bare.

Halfway down the aisle Sefa stops and speaks toward the far end, low, the way you speak to someone whose name you haven't learned yet.

"Peace to you. I'm Sefa, from the hospice in the Lower City. Kesh heard you calling, two nights. I'm sorry no one came sooner."

Nothing answers her. She walks the rest of the way and crouches near the boots.

He sits against the back wall between the last two shelves with his legs out toward the door, which is why the boot soles showed first. His head has fallen forward onto his chest. Ash has settled on his hair and shoulders and on the folds of a buff leather coat, like grey snow on a fence-post.

He was a big man, past forty, with a short beard gone stiff. The left leg is the one that dragged. The boot on that side is burned through at the ankle, and the breeches above it are charred to the knee and stuck to what's under them. A waterskin lies beside his hip, flat and dry. He's dead. The skin of his face is drawn tight and brown over the bones, and there's hardly any smell.

His right hand is closed into a fist against his breastbone. The light comes from there, leaking out between the fingers, white-gold and steady, like the top step at evening. In the cracks of his knuckles the skin is black, iron-black. Ash lies everywhere else on him, but none has settled on that fist. It looks clean, as if he'd closed it a moment ago.

A fold of paper stands out of the breast of his coat above the fist, its edge grey with ash.

Beside his left hand the ash has been scraped away down to the stone in a patch the size of a shield. A hobnail lies in the middle of it, worked loose from the burned boot and used as a pen. Scratched into the stone in rough, shaky capitals, in plain Common:

*DELLMERE PAYS ON DELIVERY.*
*NOBODY DELIVERS.*

*DONT LET IT GO OUT OF*

The last line stops there. The scratch of the final letter trails off down the stone and goes nowhere.

You stop a pace short of the boots with the lantern held low. The floor round the man is undisturbed apart from the cleared patch and the man's own furrow. Nothing has been moved since he stopped moving. There's no wire and no trick in it. It's a dead man in a cold room with his hand shut on a light.

Behind you, at the far end of the aisle, the doorway is a dim rectangle of passage-dark with Bram's shoulder and the edge of his shield in it, facing away.

Where you are: a pace short of the dead man at the back wall · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram keeps his back to the cold room and his face to the heat. His voice comes down the aisle low and even, and it reaches the far end because nothing else in the room makes a sound: "If that white-gold is the lamp's kin, then Arren's warning stands: nothing of the fire goes up. We look, we learn, we don't carry it." He shifts his grip on the shield. "Keep clear of the chisel and the body until you've looked at both with the light low. If he's been dead since before the Warm One came, his boots may be the only honest thing in here." He pauses, then adds: "Call if that light brightens, or if the boots aren't empty. And Sefa, if your book goes warm again, you tell me, not after." After that he says nothing more. Out on the slope the orange stays where it is on the walls.

At the back wall Sefa bows her head over the dead man and says the hospice words a second time, very low, the same short ones she said over the basket of jaws. She keeps her beads in her left hand. Then she pulls the fleece down off her mouth far enough to talk to you.

"He's been dead about a tenday. The burn on that leg, and no water. Two nights, the way Kesh said." She points at the scratched stone without touching it and reads it to you under her breath: "*Dellmere pays on delivery. Nobody delivers. Don't let it go out of...* and then it stops." She looks at the clean fist and the light leaking between his fingers. "Out of what? His hand? This room? I don't know. But he spent his last strength writing it, so we listen to him before we do anything clever."

She nods at the fold of paper in his coat. "Pell, that letter's yours. Wrapped hand, slow. See if the seal's whole and what's pressed in it. Don't break it yet, just ease it out if it comes without tearing. Dellmere's a name, and someone paid for that chisel."

Then she holds her wrapped right fist a hand's width above his fist and watches. Her Light is white and plain, a candle behind horn. The light between his fingers is warmer, white-gold. It doesn't lean toward hers or shrink away. It goes on as if hers weren't there.

"If it's what I think," she murmurs, "it was safe here because he can't see in here. The moment it's in the passage, it may be the brightest thing the Warm One has felt in years." A breath. "So we look at it here, and we decide here."

She lays her wrapped fingers over his and eases the first finger up, slowly. It gives. The second gives too. At the third a knuckle lets go with a small dry crack, and she keeps going without hurrying. Her own palm is cupped under his the whole time.

The light comes out into the room.

It's a shard of pale brass, about the size of her palm, shaped like a wedge where it broke away from something bigger. Two of its edges are bright and raw, bitten with the square marks of a chisel. The face turned up carries a tiny engraved lantern, no bigger than a thumbnail, with a ring handle and a single drop of flame. The glow comes from that drop. The break cuts right through the bottom of it, a chipped tooth, the way Kesh drew it in the air. As his fingers fall open the shard tips into her wrapped palm, and she closes her hand over it before it can touch the ash.

For those few moments in the uncovered air it spread a pale wash about ten feet round you both. It lit the spines of the nearest black books, the dead man's face and your knees, and nothing more. Now the white-gold leaks out through the wool of her fist beside her own white Light.

Your words land with the fingers already open and the shard already in her fist.

The paper isn't ash. It's good heavy rag paper that has only been sitting in a dead man's coat, and it slides free when you test the edge. The wax was broken a long time ago. The red seal split cleanly along the fold when someone opened it the first time, and the two halves still stick to either side. Pressed into the wax is a merchant's mark: an anvil with a tall D cut across its face.

You know that mark. You've seen it stencilled on iron bales on the wharves of the Gray Harbor and painted over a warehouse door down there. Dellmere is a middling iron-factoring house of the Gate. You never took a job from them, and they never had a reason to know your name.

You open it on your flat palm, keeping your other hand underneath it, and hold the lantern so Sefa can read it with you.

> *Dask —*
>
> *Terms as agreed. Forty gold on your hand tonight, the balance of one hundred and sixty on delivery, at this house or at our office on the Gray Harbor.*
>
> *East of the Ulcaster stones, the warm hill. A stair under it, and at its foot a passage to the lower cellar. You will find a door with a lamp on it. The lamp is the lock. The chisel will answer for it.*
>
> *Open the lower cellar and bring out the book bound in iron. That, and nothing else.*
>
> *The beast below may be left to itself. Do not trouble with it.*
>
> *Burn this.*
>
> *— O. Tarr, for Dellmere Iron Factors*

He didn't burn it.

At the top, above *Dask*, a fold-line has worn through, and in the gap someone has written in pencil, smaller and later, *at the Burning Wizard, Beregost*. That's the inn on the main street there, where the caravan men drink.

As you speak, you look from the scratches on the stone to Sefa's closed fist.

Under the open coat a flat leather purse hangs on the dead man's belt, buckled shut. Nobody has touched it.

The room is as still as before. Down the length of the aisle Bram's shoulder and the rim of his shield stand in the doorway, facing out, and the white-gold in Sefa's fist is far too small to reach him.

Where you are: crouched beside Sefa at the back wall with the lantern and letter · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Sefa keeps her fist shut over the shard and lets out a long breath through the fleece. For a moment she just holds it there, eyes closed. Then she turns her head toward the door and pitches her voice up the aisle: "Bram. You said tell you, not after. The Book's warm, like a cup through cloth. It went warmer when I came near his hand. I have the light. It's a piece of the lamp, brass, chiselled off. A ward-link, still whole, still working, and it's the same light as mine. The same well. Nothing's moved in here. He's dead, a tenday, the leg and no water. Stay where you are."

She reads the letter a second time over your flat palm, slowly. Her lips move at *the lamp is the lock* and again at *the beast below may be left to itself*. She says it low: Dellmere wanted the book and never cared about the Warm One. They sent four men to cut the lock off his cage and didn't care what walked out after, and Dask understood that at the end. *Nobody delivers.* She tells you to fold the letter and keep it close.

"Dellmere. I know the mark. Iron factors back in the Gate." You fold the letter along its old creases and slip it inside your jerkin.

Then she unwinds the strip from her hand. The glow comes away with it; it was laid on the wool, not on her, and as the last turn comes off her bare fingers they go dark. Only your lantern lights her now. She opens her fist over the loose fleece and the shard lies in the white glow. As she turns it to fold the wool over, its other face comes up for the first time.

There's a tower cut into the brass, worn but plain: tall and narrow, with a squared crown and three slit windows down its face. It's the same sign as on the lintel at the mouth, and on the waystones of the east road. Ulcaster's tower is on one face and the lantern on the other. She folds the wool over both, and the white-gold disappears.

The bundle doesn't go dark, though. The wool is still glowing, white and steady like a candle behind horn. When she lays it in Dask's open palm and closes his stiff fingers over it, as far as they'll go, light shows between his knuckles again. It's whiter now than the shard's was.

"*Don't let it go out*," she murmurs to him. "We won't. Not out of this room till it goes home."

You watch the bundle go into the dead man's hand. It's already covered, and you give it one short nod.

She tells you to leave the man's coin. If there's anything in the purse with a name on it, a token or a letter for kin, you can look, but you put it back. Dask gets proper rites when this is done, not a basket. Then she starts back up the aisle in Dask's prints, keeping wide of the chisel, toward the dim shape of Bram's shield in the doorway.

Your call up the aisle goes soft and close, with no echo.

Then you turn to the purse. You check the buckle first. It's a plain brass tongue, stiff with old sweat. There's no needle, no second catch and no thread running anywhere it shouldn't. You work it loose with your wrapped hand and hold the purse open over the dead man's lap so nothing can spill into the ash.

There are twelve gold pieces and nothing else. No token, no folded note, nothing with a name on it.

The coins aren't Gate money. They're Amnian danters, the gold that comes up the Way from Athkatla, and you've handled enough coin to know them by weight and stamp in this light. They're new, too. The edges are still sharp from the mint and the faces show no wear. None of them has been clipped or bitten. If the letter is honest about forty in hand, this is what's left of the advance, and every coin looks as if it came out of the same bag on the same day.

You hold the purse open over Dask's knees.

---

From the doorway comes the sound of a broom, *shhk, shhk*, quick, and then a voice beyond it, reaching you soft and close with no echo. It's Ixx's recited voice, laid word on word, with less of Ixx in it than before.

"The Warm One says: *the wardens' room is ash. Ash says nothing worth the waiting.*"

A pause.

"*The Warm One has been patient. He said it two times. He does not say it a third.* *The shield-man sets terms to faces. Bring the faces. All three, at the door. Now.*"

Then his own voice, small and fast: "After the broom, he does not send the broom. He sends elders. Slings. Not little ones. Elders. Kesh too."

And: "Ixx sweeps you through the long room. Now?"

Where you are: at the back wall of the wardens' room, beside Dask's body · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

From the doorway, Bram's voice comes softly up the aisle, half-turned toward you and Sefa: "Close it. Leave everything where it lies, including the chisel. I don't care if it's cold iron; it belongs to the house, not to us. Sefa, wrap that brass in wool and keep it close to your body, under your belt. If it warms again, I'll know."

Sefa, at his shoulder, raises two fingers toward your end of the room. At the back wall the white between Dask's knuckles thins and goes out. Nothing shows through the wool after it. The only light left in the room is your lantern, a small yellow island at the end of the aisle.

Sefa calls softly up the aisle: "Pell. Leave the purse as it was and come. Walk his prints out, wide of the chisel. Pull the door to behind you, gently. Bronze, not iron. It won't ring."

---

You close the purse over Dask's knees and work the stiff brass tongue back through its buckle. The twelve gold stay where the dead man carried them.

You leave the wrapped bundle in the closed fist and start back up the aisle in the hobnail prints, lantern low, keeping wide of the chisel where it lies in its ring of thrown ash. Behind you the dark closes in shelf by shelf, until the room of burnt paper is black from end to end. A dead man sits somewhere in it with his hand shut on something nobody can see.

You stop in the doorway beside Sefa, without stepping out past Bram's shield. Down the slope Ixx waits, his broom's twigs down on the stone, the orange glow behind him.

Ixx answers your first question at once. "He said walk soft. Iron quiet. Skins are iron quiet. Skins are what he wants." Kesh is in no trouble over the fleeces, as far as he can see.

The second question takes much longer. He looks down at the broom, then at the orange glow at the bottom of the slope.

"Kesh is eldest. Elders do what Kesh says." He stops. "Kesh does what he says."

He doesn't say anything for a while. When he does speak, it's quieter.

"Before Kesh, there was another eldest. When he came down. That one said no." He says nothing about what came after. His eyes stay on the glow.

At your last words Ixx looks up at you. "Ixx neither."

Then he turns to face down the slope, sets the twigs to the groove in the floor, and stays still with the broom ready.

"Shut the black door," he says. "Then Ixx goes."

*(Out of game: the black door is still open, with you standing in it. Nobody has pulled it to yet, and Ixx won't start down until someone does.)*

Where you are: in the open black door, beside Sefa · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Bram takes half a step sideways without turning from the slope. That clears the doorway behind him, and his shield stays half-raised toward the lit wall below. He speaks over his shoulder in a voice meant for two people:

"Pell, pull it to with your hand wrapped. Once that door is shut, we don't speak of Dellmere again until we're back above ground. No names below, not his, not Arren's unless the door already has it. From here to the lamp, we give him our faces and our terms, not our store of news."

Sefa touches your sleeve, and you step back off the threshold to make room for her. She leans in at Bram's shoulder and says something to him, too low for you to catch. Then she reaches past you and takes the green bronze ring in her bare hand. She lifts as she draws, the way you did, so the foot of the door won't drag. The hinges give their one low dry note. She keeps pulling until the finger-wide gap is gone, then lowers the ring onto the oak without a sound. For a moment her palm rests flat on the char beside the dragged print, close to it but not touching.

Your whisper comes just after the latch. Your wrapped hand had gone out toward the door. You let it drop.

*(Out of game: Sefa's paragraph came first, so she shut the door. You find it done.)*

With the door shut the passage closes back in. The hum returns as if a mill-wheel had been put back in gear, and the heat leans on all three of you from below.

Bram speaks down the slope: "Now, Ixx. We step where you step. Slow at the four, wide around them. If you feel anything shift underfoot, you stop and we stop. Lead."

Ten feet down the slope Ixx looks at the shut door, and something in his shoulders lets go.

"Shut," he says.

Sefa turns to him. "Shut. Go on, Ixx. Eleven holes, four light, round them wide. When you stop, we stop. And thank you for telling Pell about the other eldest. We'll keep it at words."

His snout dips once. He doesn't look up. "Words," he says. "Good."

You take your place behind Bram, and Sefa falls in last behind you. Ixx turns, puts his twigs to the groove in the floor, and goes. *Shhk, shhk.*

Bram keeps to Ixx's line, slowly, with the hot wall a pace off his right shoulder. As he passes the bright niche he turns his shield toward it. He does it out of habit, putting the shield where the trouble is.

Nobody wrapped the shield. Its iron rim swings in a short arc and taps the rings of his mail skirt below the fleece at his hip. It makes one small, clear *chink*, iron on iron, no louder than a coin dropped on a counter. In that room it carries.

The seam in the niche goes from dull red to orange to yellow in the space of a breath.

The shape uncurls. It's a little figure of cooled slag, knee-high to Bram. Its arms are too long and end in blunt stubs, and fire runs in its cracks the way water runs in a gutter. Two holes in its lumpy head glow like the mouths of a bellows. It doesn't climb out yet. It hunches on the lip of the niche, five feet from Bram's hip, with its head turned toward him, swinging slowly from side to side like a dog trying to place a sound. Heat rolls off it in a wave.

Further along the wall, two other niches brighten. They don't wake. The sleepers in them turn over.

Ixx has stopped dead ten feet ahead with his broom lifted off the stone. He doesn't turn around. His voice comes back thin and fast, barely louder than the hum.

"Still. Stone still. He looks for the ring." A short breath. "Ring again, he comes. Ring again, they all come."

Your lantern pool lies steady on the floor, and behind you Sefa has stopped with her foot already down. The thing on the lip of the niche keeps turning its head, slowly, listening for the next sound.

Where you are: on the slope behind Bram, lantern low · Time: Day 1 · afternoon

Nobody moves.

Ahead of you Bram stays where the chink caught him, the shield still hanging at the angle it swung to. He doesn't pull it back. Sweat runs from his hairline into the fleece at his collar. His sword hand rests on the hilt and stays there. Five feet from his hip the slag-thing hunches on the lip of its niche, and its head keeps swinging, slow, from side to side.

You stand with both feet planted and the lantern held out from your body, so its bail can't touch anything. Sefa has stopped mid-step with her weight on the foot that came down, her right hand low and open at her side.

Ten feet ahead, Ixx holds his broom off the stone.

The head swings left, toward the hot wall and away from Bram, and stops there. The bellows-holes in its face flare once. Then it turns back the other way, slower, until those two glowing holes point at the fleece on Bram's hip. It leans out over the edge of the niche, a finger's width, then another.

It sniffs. It's a dry, crackling draw of air, like a fire pulling at a chimney. Whatever it's looking for is iron that rings, and what it finds is wet goat.

The crack-light along its arms dims from yellow to orange. Its long arms draw in. It settles back onto the stone, folds itself down the way a dog turns round before it lies, and pulls its head in until the head is only a lump of slag among the others. The seam in the niche goes from yellow to orange to the dull red it was before. Further along the wall the two brightened niches dim with it, one and then the other, and the sleepers in them stay asleep.

Bram turns his head a fraction, just enough to get you and Sefa into the edge of his sight. He shapes two words with no sound behind them: *when I move.*

Ixx waits a long moment more with the broom held off the floor. Then he lets out a breath through his snout, so quietly it's barely there. He doesn't look round.

"Sleeps." It's thinner than a whisper. "Again light. Not deep."

He sets the twigs down on the stone with great care, beyond the cartwheel edge of the fourth hole, where the heat above the vent shimmers like water. *Shhk.* Then he takes one step on the far side of it and stops again, exactly where he said he would. He's waiting for the tall ones to go round the hole wide the way he did.

*(Out of game: the burning one settled back on its own. Your stillness gave it nothing to find, and no fight has opened.)*

Where you are: behind Bram with the lantern in the long vent room · Time: Day 1 · evening

Bram moves first, round the hole the way Ixx went, wide, keeping to the edge of the heat. He holds the shield flat and still against his body and doesn't let it swing toward the niche this time. The air over the vent ripples like water over a weir and comes up hot enough to make your eyes sting. He takes it slowly, one foot down, weight on, then the next. The mail rustles faintly under his wool, and nothing chinks.

You follow a long stride back, the lantern held out on a straight arm. Hardly anyone on the Wide would have heard you.

Sefa comes last, setting each boot down heel first and slow. Her eyes stay on the broom. The lump of slag in the fourth niche, its seam banked back to dull red, doesn't stir as she passes.

Ixx lets you all close up behind him. Then he puts the twigs down and moves on, *shhk*, about twenty feet, and stops at his next mark. It's well short of the middle hole, a broad mouth in the floor with heat standing over it. To its left a niche glows the dull red of a coal that hasn't quite gone out. That's one of the light sleepers. The far arch is beyond it, with the last sleeper beside it, and past that the white-gold pulses slow and steady.

While you wait at the mark, Sefa closes the two steps to you and reaches past you to touch Bram's elbow, once. She pulls a fold of fleece from under her belt, the piece that was covering the worst of her studs, and presses it into his free hand. She nods at the iron rim of his shield and breathes something to him, too quiet for you to catch over the hum. Then she drops back to the end of the line with her left palm flat over the bare studs at her waist.

Up ahead, Ixx has turned his head. He sees the fleece go from her hand to Bram's, and his eyes go to the shield rim. He doesn't speak and he doesn't move off yet. He's waiting, with the twigs resting on the stone, for the tall ones to be ready.

Bram stands in the heat with the loose fold of goat wool in his hand, and the middle sleeper's niche glows twenty feet ahead.

*(Out of game: the crossing past the last two light sleepers is waiting on what Bram does with the fleece.)*

Where you are: long room, at Ixx's mark short of the middle hole · Time: Day 1 · evening

Sefa stays where she stopped, two steps behind you, her left palm flat over the bare studs at her waist and her right hand loose at her side.

Bram takes the fold of fleece. Before he can lower the shield to the floor, Sefa steps up on his shield side and holds out both hands low, palms up. He looks at them for half a breath, then sets the iron rim down on her palms instead of on the stone. Leather and skin take its weight without a sound.

He works fast. He pulls the wool over the rim in short, hard tucks, a hand's width at a time, all the way round, and works the fleece down into the gap between rim and oak so it can't ride up. He has no gut left to tie it with, so he jams the last fold under the grip-strap and pulls the strap tight on top of it. You keep the lantern clear and low the whole time, its light on his hands and nowhere else, and watch the middle niche over his shoulder. The dull red glow in the niche doesn't change.

Bram lifts the shield off Sefa's palms, turns it flat against his side and pulls his elbow in. He tests it once against his hip. Fleece meets fleece with a soft hush, and nothing rings.

Sefa goes back to her place two steps behind you. Her left palm is back over the bare studs at her waist, and her lips move with some count.

Bram gives Ixx one slow nod. Without turning, he breathes something to Sefa, too low for you to catch.

Ixx's eyes go over the wrapped rim once. Then he sets the twigs down. *Shhk.*

He leads you left of the middle hole, close under the glowing wall and wide of the heat that stands over the vent. The niche of the middle sleeper is right there at shoulder height, an arm's length off Bram's shield side.

Bram gets three steps past the mouth of the middle niche, and it's his mail that gives him away, not the shield. His sword arm is the one part of him the fleeces don't cover. As he draws his elbow in to keep the shield flat, the rings of his sleeve slide over the rings at his ribs with a short dry rasp. It's iron grinding on iron, quieter than the chink at the fourth hole, but it happens right beside a sleeper that sleeps light.

The niche flares. It goes from dull red to yellow with nothing in between.

This one doesn't stop on the lip to listen. It uncurls and comes out at once, all its too-long arms first, and drops to the floor between Bram and the wall with a soft crunch, like a cinder landing on a hearth. It's the same kind of thing as the first, knee-high cooled slag with fire running in its cracks. Its two bellows-holes turn up to Bram. It sniffs. Its head swings past the fleece at his hip and stops at his bare sword arm, and the light in its cracks goes from yellow toward white.

It lifts one blunt stub and reaches toward his elbow. It hasn't touched him yet. Where the heat off it leans against the greasy fleece at his hip, the wool starts to curl and smoke, and the smell of scorched goat fills the air.

Behind you, back by the fourth hole, the bright niche brightens again, though nothing comes out of it. Ahead, by the far arch, the last sleeper's niche goes from red to orange and stays there.

Ten feet ahead, Ixx has turned all the way round this time with the broom held off the stone. His voice comes thin and fast.

"Wool burns. Grease burns." His eyes go to the smoking fleece and then to the stub reaching for Bram's arm. "He wants the iron under. He touches, iron gets hot, *you* burn."

The burning one's stub hangs a hand's width from Bram's elbow, and the fleece at his hip has started to smoke. You are right behind Bram with the lantern, and Sefa is two steps behind you. None of you has moved yet.

Where you are: right behind Bram with the lantern · Time: Day 1 · evening
